question: Does the published \unilid-Mistral WiLI row use the mistralai/Mistral-Nemo-Base-2407 tokenizer (author's belief, 2026-08-23), or a 32k Mistral-7B tokenizer (the plan's designation)?

paper_evidence.corpus: WiLI (trained on WiLI, evaluated on WiLI)
paper_evidence.caption_verbatim: Macro-averaged F1 and FPR of different LID systems on WiLI; \camrev{the rows below the dashed line} are variants of \unilid trained using the base tokenizers from open-source LLMs.
paper_evidence.duplicate_in_initial_version: paper/initial_version.tex:1302-1303, identical cells; its caption reads 'the latter 4 systems are variants of \unilid trained using the base tokenizers from open-source LLMs' (stale: six rows sit below the dashed line)

other_mistral_mentions.paper/tables/lid_main.tex:82: \unilid-Mistral-Nemo row, GlotLID-C / UDHR / FLORES-200 corpora (GlotLID-C-trained). No \unilid-Mistral row exists there.
other_mistral_mentions.paper/submission.tex:784: names mistralai/Mistral-Nemo-Base-2407 as the tokenizer behind \unilid-Mistral-Nemo
other_mistral_mentions.note: \unilid-Mistral appears ONLY at paper/tables/unilid_llm_comparison.tex:15 and paper/initial_version.tex:1303. The paper never names a repository for it.

paper_evidence.per_model_vocab_size_in_paper: NONE. tab:vocab_size_efficiency lists vocabulary sizes only for the dedicated-tokenizer sweep (10k/20k/50k/100k/200k), not per LLM variant. training_time and latency tables carry no vocabulary column.

recorded_reasoning_under_challenge.verbatim_1: | `\unilid-Mistral` | `mistral-community/Mistral-7B-v0.2` | **cannot be Mistral-Nemo**: the published rows differ (0.921 against 0.958), so the tokenizers differ. Vocabulary size discriminates sharply, 32,768 against 131,072 |
recorded_reasoning_under_challenge.verbatim_2: Note `\unilid-Mistral` cannot be Mistral-Nemo: the published rows differ (0.921 against 0.958).
recorded_reasoning_under_challenge.validity: VALID. The two cells are adjacent rows of one table, one corpus (WiLI), one training recipe; the caption states the rows differ only in base tokenizer. Equal tokenizer would imply equal cells. The elliptical phrasing hid this premise, but the premise holds.
recorded_reasoning_under_challenge.error_inside_it: the parenthetical '32,768 against 131,072' is wrong: mistral-community/Mistral-7B-v0.2 has 32,000 entries (measured). 32,768 is Mistral-7B-v0.3. Already recorded as an open author question at SESSION_STATUS.md:130-132.

comparison_a_nemo_vs_container.verdict: MEASURED: the GlotLID-C Mistral-Nemo container's base vocabulary IS mistralai/Mistral-Nemo-Base-2407, exact ordered identity.

comparison_b_mistral7b_v02.normalizer: Prepend U+2581 + Replace space -> U+2581 (SentencePiece style, byte-fallback <0xNN> tokens)
comparison_b_mistral7b_v02.verdict: MEASURED: entirely different vocabulary from Nemo (32,000 vs 131,072; 10,172 shared surface forms; different pre-tokenization regime).

mistral_repo_family.implication: MEASURED: v0.1 and community v0.2 are the SAME vocabulary, so the v0.1-vs-v0.2 half of the open author question is moot. v0.3 is genuinely different and would be a different model.

vocab_size_vs_published_f1.note: vocabulary sizes MEASURED from the extracted/downloaded base tokenizers; F1 from tab:unilid_llm_comparison
vocab_size_vs_published_f1.pattern: INFERRED: every >=128k byte-level vocabulary lands at 0.949-0.958; the only two sub-0.93 rows (0.911, 0.921) are exactly the two 32k non-byte-level SentencePiece vocabularies. A Nemo-tokenizer model landing at 0.921 would contradict the 0.958 Nemo row in the same table.

verdict.surviving_hypothesis: (ii) \unilid-Mistral is a 32k Mistral-7B tokenizer, NOT Mistral-Nemo-Base-2407. The author's belief does not survive.
discriminating_evidence: 0.921 and 0.958 are rows 15 and 14 of ONE table on ONE corpus with one recipe varying only the base tokenizer (paper/tables/unilid_llm_comparison.tex:11-22).
The paper names Mistral-Nemo-Base-2407 explicitly for the \unilid-Mistral-Nemo row (submission.tex:784) and gives \unilid-Mistral its own separate row.
MEASURED F1-vs-vocabulary pattern: 0.921 sits with the 32k SentencePiece cluster, not the 131k byte-level cluster.
verdict.residual_open_question: WHICH 32k Mistral repository. v0.1 and community-v0.2 are byte-identical (32,000) and interchangeable; v0.3 (32,768) is not. The repo evidence cannot choose between the 32,000 and 32,768 families - author information only.
verdict.only_way_author_is_right: a labelling error in the published table (a row printed as \unilid-Mistral that was actually run with the Nemo vocabulary under some other differing setting), which would make the table self-contradictory - two Nemo rows differing by 0.037 F1. No repo artefact supports this.
verdict.job_3161886_targets: the \unilid-Mistral-Nemo WiLI row (0.958 / 1.925e-4) in tab:unilid_llm_comparison, which is a distinct published row. Mistral-Nemo also carries GlotLID-C rows (lid_main.tex:82, calibrated_nemo.tex:10). The job does not target the \unilid-Mistral row.
